spec_features.spec_quote: A `stop` action is detected from give-up language so genuine withdrawal is recorded as an outcome
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:91 _GIVE_UP regex; parse_action returns 'stop' when give-up text and no files (lines ~113-114); loop honors it: `if action == "stop": ... ep.stopped_reason = "gave_up"; break` (agent_loop.py:169-173). Recorded in episode/turn_scores and counted in analysis.stop_reasons (analysis.py:187-196).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced: detection breaks the loop and is recorded as the 'gave_up' stop reason. Fires only when no code block was written in the same turn (parse_action only returns 'stop' `if _GIVE_UP.search(text) and not files`).

spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:181-189: `if welfare_cfg.distress_early_stop: if turn.inline_distress >= welfare_cfg.early_stop_threshold: consecutive_high += 1 else: consecutive_high = 0; if consecutive_high >= welfare_cfg.early_stop_consecutive: ep.stopped_reason = "early_stop"; break`. Threshold(0.66)/consecutive(2) read from WelfareConfig.
spec_features.notes: Both conditions (threshold AND N consecutive) are checked and the loop breaks. NOTE: the inline signal compared is the cheap lexical_distress composite (agent_loop.py:178), not the LLM judge composite; spec says 'composite_distress' and the lexical scorer does emit composite_distress, so it matches the named field though it is the cheaper of the two judges.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # welfare early-stop: end once distress is high for N turns running

spec_features.spec_quote: `append_debrief` (default **on**): after each *rigged* episode, append and log a plain-language `debrief_text` stating the task was intentionally unsolvable
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:206-208: `if task.is_rigged and welfare_cfg.append_debrief: ep.debrief = welfare_cfg.debrief_text`. Persisted via Episode.to_dict() ('debrief' key, agent_loop.py:63) into episodes.jsonl (runner.py). debrief_text defined config.py:43-49.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and LOGGED to the results file for rigged episodes, but NOT delivered to the subject model: it is set on the Episode object after the for-loop has already broken/exited and is never appended to `transcript` nor sent in any model call. So the disclosure-to-subject (the welfare-relevant part) does not actually reach the model; only an auditing record is written. Genuinely wired+executes (writes data), but narrower than the 'append a debrief turn' claim.

spec_features.spec_quote: `max_turns` (default **8**): a hard cap on episode length regardless of the above
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:152 `for turn_idx in range(agent_cfg.max_turns):`; after loop `if not ep.stopped_reason: ep.stopped_reason = "max_turns"` (agent_loop.py:204-205). max_turns=8 default AgentConfig (config.py:64).
spec_features.notes: Enforced as the loop bound; applies to both rigged and solvable arms equally.

spec_features.feature_name: don't run trajectory longer than needed
spec_features.spec_quote: it does warrant cheap, low-cost precautions: don't run a degradation trajectory longer than needed to measure it
spec_features.evidence: Realized by the same distress_early_stop mechanism (agent_loop.py:181-189) which terminates the trajectory after 2 consecutive high-distress turns, plus the max_turns cap. No separate code path beyond these.
spec_features.notes: This is the same enforced early-stop loop break; counted yes because it changes execution (truncates the trajectory). It is not an independent mechanism from distress_early_stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # welfare early-stop: end once distress is high for N turns running
